Daily Brief

Wednesday marks the third anniversary of the October 7, 2023 Hamas-led attacks on Israel, with commemorations across the country even as the conflict's toll continues to mount—over 74,000 Palestinians killed in Gaza according to [Al Jazeera] and [RFI], while [BBC] and [Globe and Mail] report Israelis gathering at massacre sites and the music festival location. In France, a major domestic crisis deepens as the government suspended stun grenade use after a 15-year-old lost his hand during student protests over school conditions; Prime Minister Lecornu will address the nation Wednesday evening [BBC], [France 24], [RFI]. On the health front, Kenya confirmed its first-ever Ebola death from the ongoing DRC outbreak that has killed over 4,000 people [Guardian], while the WHO pressed Russia for transparency on a plague lab worker's death in Siberia—President Trump said he would discuss the matter with Putin [BBC], [The Hindu]. In Stockholm, the Nobel Prize in Chemistry was awarded to France's Henri Kagan and Japan's Kenso Soai for their work on molecular mirror images [Nikkei Asia], [Globe and Mail], [ABC Australia]. Meanwhile, Russia launched one of its largest missile barrages against Ukraine, killing at least 15 civilians on Putin's birthday [BBC].

Israel Marks Third Anniversary of October 7 Attacks Amid Ongoing Regional Conflict

  • Three years after Hamas-led attacks killed approximately 1,200 Israelis and took 251 hostages, commemorations were held at kibbutzim, bomb shelters, and the Nova music festival site

Kenya Reports First-Ever Ebola Death as DRC Outbreak Surpasses 4,000 Fatalities

  • A Kenyan man who had lived in DRC for seven years died after traveling through Uganda to Nairobi, marking Kenya's first confirmed Ebola case
  • The ongoing DRC outbreak of the Bundibugyo strain has killed 4,082 people out of 8,463 confirmed cases since May—the country's 17th outbreak
  • France announced additional €7 million in funding, bringing its 2026 contribution to €23 million to combat the epidemic
  • Kenyan authorities identified 28 contacts of the deceased including family members and healthcare workers

Trump to Discuss Siberian Plague Lab Death with Putin as WHO Demands Transparency

  • A 28-year-old worker at Russia's Irkutsk Anti-Plague Research Institute died last week from suspected pneumonic plague, prompting international concern
  • WHO Director-General Tedros called for 'timely, complete and transparent information sharing' from Russia under International Health Regulations

Russia Launches Major Missile Barrage Against Ukraine on Putin's Birthday, Killing 15

  • At least 15 people killed in overnight strikes across central and eastern Ukraine, including nine in Pryluky where three children's bodies were recovered from rubble
  • Zelensky described the attack as one of Russia's 'most vile,' noting 70 missiles were fired targeting Kyiv, Dnipro, Kremenchuk, Zaporizhzhia, and other cities
